verses.text: Be careful to obey every command I am giving you today. Then you will live, grow in number, and go in and take over the land the LORD promised your ancestors.

Remember how the LORD your God led you all the way through the desert these forty years. He did it to humble you and test you, to find out what was in your heart, whether you would keep his commands or not.

He humbled you by letting you go hungry, and then he fed you with manna, food that neither you nor your ancestors had ever known. He did this to teach you that people do not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of the LORD.
During these forty years your clothes did not wear out, and your feet did not swell.
So understand in your heart that the LORD your God trains and corrects you, just as a father trains and corrects his son.
Obey the commands of the LORD your God. Live the way he wants, and fear him.
For the LORD your God is bringing you into a good land, a land with streams and springs, with water flowing from deep under the ground into the valleys and hills.
It is a land of wheat and barley, of grapevines, fig trees, and pomegranates, a land of olive oil and honey.
In that land you will have plenty of food to eat and will not lack anything. Its rocks have iron in them, and you can dig copper out of its hills.
When you have eaten and are full, praise the LORD your God for the good land he has given you.
Be careful that you do not forget the LORD your God by failing to keep his commands, laws, and rules that I am giving you today.
When you have eaten and are full, when you have built fine houses and live in them,
when your herds and flocks grow large, when your silver and gold increase, and everything you own grows,
then do not become proud and forget the LORD your God, who brought you out of Egypt, the land where you were slaves.
He led you through the huge and terrible desert, with its poisonous snakes and scorpions, a dry land with no water. He made water flow for you out of hard rock.
He fed you in the desert with manna, which your ancestors had never known. He did this to humble you and test you, so that in the end it would go well with you.
Do not say to yourself, "I got all this wealth by my own power and strength."
But remember the LORD your God, for he is the one who gives you the ability to become rich. He does this to keep the covenant he promised your ancestors, as he is doing today.
If you ever forget the LORD your God and follow other gods, serving them and bowing down to them, I warn you today that you will surely be destroyed.
Just like the nations the LORD is destroying ahead of you, you too will be destroyed, because you would not obey the LORD your God.
